BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r5.claim: He links this surah to earlier warnings about human ignorance and injustice and cites the ungrateful person, humanity in loss, and the man who thinks wealth makes him immortal.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r5.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما تضمنت السور المتقدمة من الوعيد لمن انطوى على ما ذكر فيها

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas explains kanud as ungrateful.

DURR-FULL:v8p602/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r2.claim: Qatada reads the passage as horses running until panting, striking sparks with their hooves, raiding at dawn, raising dust, entering the people’s gathering; kanud means ungrateful.
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {والعاديات ضبحا} قال: هي الخيل تعدو حتى تضبح

DURR-FULL:v8p602/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r18.claim: Ibn Abbas defines kanud as ungrateful for blessings, one who eats alone, withholds help, and starves his servant.
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r18.anchor: قال: الكنود الكفور للنعمة وهو الذي يأكل وحده ويمنع رفده ويجيع عبده

DURR-FULL:v8p602/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r19.speaker: شاعر
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r19.claim: A cited poem uses kanud for one who fails to be grateful for a gift.
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r19.anchor: أما سمعت الشاعر وهو يقول: شكرت له يوم العكاظ نواله ولم أك للمعروف ثم كنودا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r18.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r18.claim: Asked what kanud means, the Prophet calls it ingratitude: eating alone, withholding provision, and beating a servant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r18.anchor: وروي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «أتدرون ما الكنود؟ قالوا لا يا رسول الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r19.claim: The verse means that a human is deeply ungrateful for the Lord's favor; even a believer may be ungrateful for blessings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r19.anchor: وقد يكون من المؤمنين الكفور بالنعمة، فتقدير الآية: إن الإنسان لنعمة ربه لكنود،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r20.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r20.claim: Al-Hasan says kanud is one who blames his Lord, counts wrongs, and forgets good things; the word can also mean disobedient in Kinda dialect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r20.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن: الكنود اللائم لربه الذي يعد السيئات وينسى الحسنات،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r21.claim: Kanud is also used for a horse; Abu Zubayd is cited as poetic evidence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r21.anchor: والكنود العاصي بلغة كندة، ويقال للخيل كنود، وقال أبو زبيد:

TABRISI:100:4-11/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:4-11/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:100:4-11/r3.claim: Kanūd means ungrateful and denying God's blessings; Qatada, al-Hasan, and Mujahid report the same.
TABRISI:100:4-11/r3.anchor: والكنود الكفور الجحود لنعم الله عن ابن عباس وقتادة والحسن ومجاهد

TABRISI:100:4-11/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:4-11/r4.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:100:4-11/r4.claim: In Kinda and Hadramawt the word means sinner, while in Mudar, Rabiʿa, and Qudaʿa it means ungrateful.
TABRISI:100:4-11/r4.anchor: هو بلسان كندة وحضرموت العاصي وبلسان مضر وربيعة وقضاعة الكفور

TABRISI:100:4-11/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:4-11/r5.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:100:4-11/r5.claim: An ungrateful person counts his misfortunes and forgets his blessings; a quoted poem makes the same complaint.
TABRISI:100:4-11/r5.anchor: هو الذي يعد المصائب وينسى النعم عن الحسن

TABRISI:100:4-11/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:4-11/r6.speaker: أبو أمامة
TABRISI:100:4-11/r6.claim: A Prophetic report describes the ungrateful person as one who eats alone, withholds help, and beats his servant.
TABRISI:100:4-11/r6.anchor: وروى أبو أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

TABRISI:100:4-11/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:4-11/r7.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:100:4-11/r7.claim: Kanūd can mean someone who fails to give to his community in times of calamity; Abu ʿUbayda glosses it as having little good.
TABRISI:100:4-11/r7.anchor: الكنود الذي لا يعطي في النائبة مع قومه عن عطاء

TABRISI:100:4-11/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:4-11/r14.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:100:4-11/r14.claim: Abu ʿUbayda glosses kanūd as a person who has little good.
TABRISI:100:4-11/r14.anchor: هو القليل الخير عن أبي عبيدة

BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r1.claim: Kanud is the oath’s answer and means rejecting a blessing or being intensely ungrateful; Kinda’s name is linked to an ancestor who rejected favor and left his people.
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r1.anchor: جواب القسم يقال كند النعمة كنودا كفر بها فالكنود بالضم كفران النعمة

BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r2.speaker: الكلبي
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi gives regional meanings for kanud: disobedient in Kinda, stingy among Banu Malik, and ungrateful among Mudar and Rabi‘a.
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r2.anchor: الكنود بلسان كندة العاصي وبلسان بني مالك البخيل

BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r3.claim: ‘Human’ refers to some or to the human kind, and the lām in ‘to his Lord’ gives emphasis or restriction while also fitting the rhyme.
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r3.anchor: فقوله لربه متعلق بكنود قدم عليه لإفادة التخصيص

BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r4.claim: A report says the surah came after a month without news of an expedition to Banu Kinana; hypocrites claimed its members were killed, so the surah informed the Prophet of their safety and raid and reproached the rumor-mongers.
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r4.anchor: روى أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث إلى ناس من بني كنانة سرية

BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r5.claim: The oath’s ‘charging horses’ can mean the known horses of that expedition or all horses charging in God’s cause; either way their noble qualities warrant the oath, and the fighters’ merit is greater still.
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r5.anchor: فاللام في العاديات إن كانت للعهد كان المقسم به خيل تلك السرية وإن كانت للجنس كان ذلك قسما بكل خيل عدت

BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r6.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r6.claim: The Prophet defines the ungrateful person as one who beats his servant, eats alone, and withholds his gift.
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r6.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام الكنود هو الذي يضرب عبده ويأكل وحده ويمنع رفده

BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r7.claim: Hatim al-Ta’i exemplifies generosity, Abu Habahib extreme stinginess, and Ash‘ab extreme greed, illustrated by comic tales of expecting food or gifts wherever he went.
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r7.anchor: يقال كان ثلاثة نفر من العرب في عصر وحد أحدهم آية في السخاء وهو خاتم الطائي

BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r8.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says the ungrateful person complains repeatedly about misfortunes while forgetting blessings.
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن لكنود أي لوام لبه يذكر المصيبات وينسى النعم

BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r9.claim: Abu Ubayda compares kanud to barren land that yields nothing, as though the word were a reversal of nakd.
BURSEVI:v10p383#3/r9.anchor: قليل الخير من الأرض الكنود التي لا تنبت شيئا كأنه مقلوب النكد

QASHANI:100:6-11/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:100:6-11/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:100:6-11/r1.claim: Humanity is ungrateful, veiled from God by blessings, stopping at them instead of using them to reach Him.
QASHANI:100:6-11/r1.anchor: أقسم بحرمة الشاكرين لأنعمه الواصلين إليه بتواصلها على أن الإنسان لكفور لربه

SULAMI:v2p415/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p415/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p415/r2.claim: The ungrateful person rests his head on a cushion of blessing while his heart remains in heedlessness.
SULAMI:v2p415/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم في قوله : ﴿ إن الإنسان لربه لكنود ﴾ قال : رأسه على وسادة النعمة

SULAMI:v2p415/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p415/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p415/r3.claim: He notices what comes from himself but fails to see what is directed toward him.
SULAMI:v2p415/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : يرى ما منه ، ولا يرى ما إليه

SULAMI:v2p415/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p415/r4.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
SULAMI:v2p415/r4.claim: Gratitude preserves God's blessings and requires avoiding disobedience; the ungrateful count calamities and forget blessings.
SULAMI:v2p415/r4.anchor: قال عمر بن عبد العزيز : قيدوا نعم الله بالشكر ، وشكرها ترك المعصية

TUSTARI:100:6/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:100:6/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:100:6/r1.claim: The ungrateful person breaks the covenant, abandons truth, and becomes accustomed to passion, after which God makes him despair of goodness and piety.
TUSTARI:100:6/r1.anchor: قال: الكنود الكفور، وهو الذي خالف العهد وجانب الصدق وألف الهوى

FARRA:v3p285/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p285/r1.speaker: الحسن
FARRA:v3p285/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses kanūd as ungrateful to his Lord: he counts his sins and forgets blessings.
FARRA:v3p285/r1.anchor: قال الحسن: «إن الإنسان لربه لكنود» قال: لوام لربه يعد المسيئات، وينسى النعم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p536#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p536#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p536#4/r1.claim: كنود means deeply ungrateful; barren land is also called kanūd because it grows nothing.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says kanud means ungrateful in the language of the local people.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : الكنود بلساننا اهل البلد : الكفور

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458/r2.claim: Al-Hasan explains the ungrateful person as one who counts calamities while forgetting God's blessings.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458/r2.anchor: عن الحسن ان الانسان لربه لكنود قال : لكفور يعدد المصيبات وينسى نعم ربه عز وجل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p502/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p502/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p502/r1.claim: The oath's answer is that humanity is intensely ungrateful to its Lord; kanūd varies by dialect: ingrate among Mudar and Rabīʿa, miser among Kināna, disobedient among Kinda and Ḥaḍramawt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p502/r1.anchor: والكنود : وصف من أمثلة المبالغة من كند

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p502/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p502/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p502/r2.claim: The generic definite “human” often implies all humanity: self-preference innately inclines people to ingratitude, though prophets and the most complete righteous escape it through self-monitoring and recognition of others' rights.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p502/r2.anchor: وهذا عارض يعرض لكل إنسان على تفاوتت فيه ولا يسلم منه

NAHHAS:v5p278/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p278/r1.speaker: أهل التفسير
NAHHAS:v5p278/r1.claim: Exegetes take كنود to mean ungrateful for God’s favors.
NAHHAS:v5p278/r1.anchor: أهل التفسير على أن معناه لكفور أي كفور لنعمه

NAHHAS:v5p278/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p278/r2.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v5p278/r2.claim: Hasan says the person complains against his Lord and blames him for hardship while forgetting blessings.
NAHHAS:v5p278/r2.anchor: قال الحسن يتسخط على ربه جل وعز ويلومه فيما يلحقه من المصائب وينسى النعم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r1.claim: The oath’s subject is humanity’s ingratitude and denial of the Lord’s blessings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r1.anchor: هذا هو المقسم عليه، بمعنى: أنه لنعم ربه لجحود كفور

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وإبراهيم النخعي وأبو الجوزاء وغيرهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r2.claim: Numerous early authorities define the ungrateful person as a denier of blessings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد وإبراهيم النخعي، وأبو الجوزاء، وأبو العالية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r3.claim: Hasan says he counts calamities while forgetting his Lord’s blessings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r3.anchor: هو الذي يعد المصائب، وينسى نعم ربه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r4.speaker: أبو أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r4.claim: A report calls the ungrateful person one who eats alone, beats his servant, and withholds help; Ibn Kathir calls its chain weak because Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr is abandoned, while Ibn Jarir records a mawquf route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p467/r4.anchor: الكفور الذي يأكل وحده، ويضرب عبده، ويمنع رفده

KASHSHAF:100:6/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:100:6/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:100:6/r1.claim: Kanūd means ungrateful; the verb describes ingratitude for a blessing. The tribe Kinda is named from separation after a son rebelled against his father.
KASHSHAF:100:6/r1.anchor: ومنه سمي : كندة ؛ لأنه كند أباه ففارقه

KASHSHAF:100:6/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:100:6/r2.speaker: الكلبي
KASHSHAF:100:6/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī gives dialectal meanings: disobedient in Kinda, stingy among Banū Mālik, and ungrateful among Muḍar and Rabīʿah.
KASHSHAF:100:6/r2.anchor: وعن الكلبي : الكنود بلسان كندة : العاصي

KASHSHAF:100:6/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:100:6/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:100:6/r3.claim: The verse singles out ingratitude to God: failing to thank a human benefactor is easier because the benefit is near, and even the greatest human gift, parents, is slight beside God's smallest gift.
KASHSHAF:100:6/r3.anchor: لأن أجل ما أنعم به على الإنسان من مثله نعمة أبويه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r4.speaker: قتادة والضحاك وابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r4.claim: They gloss كنود as ungrateful; a verse by al-A'sha depicts it as ungrateful to customary visitors.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r4.anchor: لكفور قاله قتادة , والضحاك , وابن جبير , ومنه قول الأعشى

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r5.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r5.claim: He describes the ungrateful person as complaining to God about misfortunes while forgetting blessings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r5.anchor: اللوام لربه , يذكر المصائب وينسى النعم , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r6.claim: Another gloss is one who denies the truth; the name Kinda is said to derive from denial of its ancestor, as in Ibrahim ibn Zuhayr's verse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r6.anchor: أن الكنود الجاحد للحق , وقيل إنما سميت كندة لأنها جحدت أباها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r7.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r7.claim: In the language of Kinda and Hadramawt, كنود means disobedient.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r7.anchor: أن الكنود العاصي بلسان كندة وحضرموت , وذكره يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r8.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r8.claim: He notes regional usage: Kinda and Hadramawt say disobedient, Mudar and Rabi'a say ungrateful, and Malik ibn Kinanah says miserly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r8.anchor: الكلبي : الكنود بلسان كندة وحضرموت : العاصي , وبلسان مضر وربيعة : الكفور

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r9.claim: The ungrateful person spends God's blessings in acts of disobedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r9.anchor: ينفق نعم الله في معاصي الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r10.speaker: أبو أمامة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r10.claim: A Prophetic report defines كنود as one who strikes his servant, eats alone, and withholds his generosity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r10.anchor: ما رواه القاسم عن أبي أمامه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : الكنود الذي يضرب عبده ويأكل وحده ويمنع رفده

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r11.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r11.claim: He says the verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p325/r11.anchor: الضحاك : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

MUJAHID:v2p777/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p777/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p777/r1.claim: He glosses كنود as ungrateful and disbelieving.
MUJAHID:v2p777/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال الكنود الكفور

MUJAHID:v2p777/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p777/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p777/r2.claim: He also glosses كنود as ungrateful and disbelieving; the book transmits this explanation twice.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p353#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p353#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p353#6/r1.claim: Kanūd means intensely ungrateful, especially for the Lord's blessing.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p353#6/r1.anchor: لكفور أى أنه لنعمة ربه خصوصا لشديد الكفران

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r1.claim: The verse answers the oath by saying people are disposed to deny God's blessings.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r1.anchor: هذا جواب القسم أي طبع الإنسان على كفران النعمة.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Hasan define kanud as ungrateful and denying God's favors; such a person remembers troubles and forgets blessings.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: { لكنود } لكفور جحود لنعم الله. وكذلك قال الحسن.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r3.claim: An anonymous poem rebukes someone who complains of misfortunes while forgetting blessings.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r3.anchor: إلى متى أنت وحتى متى تشكو المصيبات وتنسى النعم!

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r4.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r4.claim: Abu Umamah al-Bahili transmits a Prophetic explanation: the kanud eats alone, withholds hospitality, and beats his servant.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r4.anchor: الكنود، هو الذي يأكل وحده، ويمنع رفده، ويضرب عبده

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r5.claim: Another Prophetic report from Ibn ʿAbbas calls a person who lives alone, withholds generosity, and beats a servant among the worst people.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r5.anchor: من نزل وحده، ومنع رفده، وجلد عبده

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas gives dialectal meanings: disobedient in Kinda and Hadramawt, ungrateful in Rabiʿah and Mudar, and miserly or harsh in Kinanah.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r6.anchor: وقد روي عن ابن عباس أيضا أنه قال: الكنود بلسان كندة وحضرموت: العاصي

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r7.claim: A poem uses kanud for someone ungrateful for people's kindness; other glosses include denying little good and failing to thank for much.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r7.anchor: وقال الشاعر: كنود لنعماء الرجال ومن يكن كنودا لنعماء الرجال يبعد

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r8.claim: One etymology says Kinda denied its father; another derives kanud from cutting the bond of gratitude, supported by al-Aʿsha's rope poem.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r8.anchor: وقيل: إنما سميت كندة كندة، لأنها جحدت أباها.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r9.speaker: إبراهيم بن هرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r9.claim: Ibrahim ibn Harmah uses kanud in a poem about a miserly woman.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r9.anchor: وقال إبراهيم بن هرمة الشاعر: دع البخلاء إن شمخوا وصدوا

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r10.speaker: الأعشى
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r10.claim: Al-Aʿsha uses the root for cutting and again for ingratitude toward a visitor's customary affection.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r10.anchor: قال الأعشى: أميطي تميطي بصلب الفؤاد وصول حبال وكنادها

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the human here is an unbeliever; barren earth is also called kanud because it grows nothing.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الإنسان هنا الكافر يقول إنه لكفور ومنه الأرض الكنود

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r12.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r12.anchor: وقال الضحاك: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r13.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r13.claim: Al-Mubarrad defines kanud as one who withholds what is owed, and cites poetry by Kathir for the usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r13.anchor: قال المبرد: الكنود: المانع لما عليه.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r14.speaker: أبو بكر الواسطي وأبو بكر الوراق
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r14.claim: Al-Wasiti says the kanud spends God's gifts in disobedience; al-Warraq says he credits blessings to himself and helpers.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r14.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الواسطي: الكنود: الذي ينفق نعم الله في معاصي الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r15.speaker: الترمذي وذو النون المصري
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r15.claim: Al-Tirmidhi says the kanud sees blessings but not their Giver; Dhu al-Nun calls him anxious in hardship and withholding in ease.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r15.anchor: وقال الترمذي: الذي يرى النعمة ولا يرى المنعم.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r16.claim: Other views call the kanud envious, resentful, or ignorant of his worth; the author says all glosses return to ingratitude and the Prophet's interpretation is strongest if sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:6/r16.anchor: قلت: هذه الأقوال كلها ترجع إلى معنى الكفران والجحود.

QUTB-ZILAL:100:6/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:6/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:6/r1.claim: Quṭb says humans deny their Lord’s favors and generous beneficence; this ingratitude appears in varied words and deeds.
QUTB-ZILAL:100:6/r1.anchor: إن الإنسان ليجحد نعمة ربه ، وينكر جزيل فضله . ويتمثل كنوده وجحوده في مظاهر شتى تبدو منه أفعالا وأقوالا

RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r1.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains kanūd as withholding what is due of right and good; barren land is called kanūd because it grows nothing.
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r1.anchor: قال الواحدي : أصل الكنود منع الحق والخير والكنود الذي يمنع ما عليه ، والأرض الكنود هي التي لا تنبت شيئا

RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، عكرمة، الضحاك، قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r2.claim: They gloss kanūd as intensely ungrateful; the word is likened to Kinda, said to have left after disobeying its father.
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة والضحاك وقتادة : الكنود هو الكفور قالوا : ومنه سمي الرجل المشهور كندة لأنه كند أباه ففارقه

RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī says kanūd means disobedient in Kinda's language; the passage also gives dialect meanings of miser for Banū Mālik and ungrateful for Muḍar and Rabīʿa.
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r3.anchor: وعن الكلبي الكنود بلسان كندة العاصي وبلسان بني مالك البخيل ، وبلسان مضر وربيعة الكفور

RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r4.speaker: أبو أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet defines kanūd as an ingrate who withholds his support, eats alone, and beats his servant.
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r4.anchor: وروى أبو أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن : { * الكنود } هو الكفور الذي يمنع رفده ، ويأكل وحده ، ويضرب عبده

RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the kanūd person complains against his Lord, recounting hardships while forgetting blessings and ease, as in 89:16.
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن : { * الكنود } اللوام لربه يعد المحن والمصائب ، وينسى النعم والراحات ، وهو كقوله : { وأما إذا ما ابتلاه * ربه * فقدره * عليه رزقه * فيقول ربى أهانن }

RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r6.claim: Kanūd cannot mean anything beyond unbelief or disobedience.
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r6.anchor: واعلم أن معنى الكنود لا يخرج عن أن يكون كفرا أو فسقا

RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r7.claim: The word cannot apply to every person unless it describes a human disposition overcome only by God's protection; the alternative is a particular unbeliever.
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r7.anchor: فلا يمكن حمله على كل الناس ، فلا بد من صرفه إلى كافر معين ، أو إن حملناه على الكل كان المعنى أن طبع الإنسان يحمله على ذلك إلا إذا عصمه الله بلطفه وتوفيقيه من ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r8.claim: Most exegetes take it of a particular unbeliever; Ibn ʿAbbās reports revelation about Qurṭ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Nawfal al-Qurashī.
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r8.anchor: والأول قول الأكثرين قالوا : لأن ابن عباس قال : إنها نزلت في قرط بن عبد الله بن عمرو بن نوفل القرشي

RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r9.claim: The following question about graves being scattered fits an unbeliever, since it indicates denial of the Resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v32p63#2/r9.anchor: وأيضا فقوله : { أفلا يعلم إذا بعثر ما فى القبور } لا يليق إلا بالكافر ، لأن ذلك كالدلالة على أنه منكر لذلك الأمر

STUDYQURAN:100:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:100:6/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:100:6/r1.claim: This statement answers the oaths in the first five verses.
STUDYQURAN:100:6/r1.anchor: This verse constitutes the response to the oaths in the first five verses.

STUDYQURAN:100:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:100:6/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:100:6/r2.claim: Kanūd means either barren land where nothing grows or a petty, miserly person.
STUDYQURAN:100:6/r2.anchor: Kanūd, here translated ungrateful, indicates a land where nothing grows or a person who is petty and miserly.

SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r1.claim: إِنَّ الإنسان is the oath’s assertion, and لربه is attached to the predicate and placed first to preserve the verse endings.
SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r1.anchor: هذا هو المقسم عليه و " لربه " متعلق بالخبر، وقدم للفواصل

SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r2.claim: The author glosses الكنود as الجحود and reports the alternative gloss الكفور النعمة.

SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r3.claim: An unattributed poetic couplet cites كنود in the context of ingratitude for people’s favors.
SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r3.anchor:
وأنشد:
4628 كنود لنعماء الرجال ومن يكن

SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports regional senses: disobedient in Kinda and Ḥaḍramawt, ungrateful in Rabīʿa and Muḍar, and miserly in Kināna.
SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: هو بلسان كندة وحضرموت العاصي، وبلسان ربيعة ومضر الكفور، وبلسان كنانة البخيل

SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r5.speaker: أبو زيد
SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r5.claim: Abū Zayd cites a poetic line containing كنود as further Arabic usage evidence for the word.
SAMIN-DURR:100:6/r5.anchor:
وأنشد أبو زيد:
4629 إن تفتني فلم أطب عنك نفسا

TAB-FULL:v24p584/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the horses and riders enter the enemy host’s middle, with three forms of wasata equivalent; he glosses kanūd as ungrateful to the Lord’s favors.
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r1.anchor: وقوله: {إن الإنسان لربه لكنود} [العاديات: 6] يقول: إن الإنسان لكفور لنعم ربه.

TAB-FULL:v24p584/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r2.claim: Kanūd earth is earth that grows nothing; al-Ṭabarī quotes al-Aʿshā in the lexical discussion.
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r2.anchor: والأرض الكنود: التي لا تنبت شيئا، قال الأعشى: [البحر الكامل]

TAB-FULL:v24p584/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r3.speaker: الأعشى
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r3.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s verse uses kand in a line about a woman withholding connection from the habitual visitor, as poetic evidence accompanying the gloss of kanūd.
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r3.anchor:
قال الأعشى: [البحر الكامل]
أحدث لها تحدث لوصلك إنها … كند لوصل الزائر المعتاد

TAB-FULL:v24p584/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r4.claim: One explanation says the tribe Kinda was named because it cut off its father.
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r4.anchor: وقيل: إنما سميت كندة: لقطعها أباها.

TAB-FULL:v24p584/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, as transmitted by Mujāhid, glosses kanūd as ungrateful.
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إن الإنسان لربه لكنود} [العاديات: 6] قال: «لكفور»

TAB-FULL:v24p584/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r6.speaker: الحسن البصري
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the ungrateful person blames his Lord, counting afflictions while forgetting blessings.
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r6.anchor: عن الحسن البصري: {إن الإنسان لربه لكنود} [العاديات: 6] قال: «هو الكفور الذي يعد المصائب، وينسى نعم ربه»

TAB-FULL:v24p584/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r7.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r7.anchor: عن أبي جعفر، عن الربيع، قال: " الكنود: الكفور "

TAB-FULL:v24p584/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p584/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، {إن الإنسان لربه لكنود} [العاديات: 6] قال: «لكفور»

TAB-FULL:v24p587/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p587/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v24p587/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet describes the ungrateful person as one who eats alone, beats his servant, and withholds hospitality.
TAB-FULL:v24p587/r1.anchor: عن أبي أمامة، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " {إن الإنسان لربه لكنود} [العاديات: 6] قال: «لكفور، الذي يأكل وحده ويضرب عبده، ويمنع رفده»

TAB-FULL:v24p587/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p587/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p587/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses kanūd as ungrateful and cites 22:66, which calls the human ungrateful.
TAB-FULL:v24p587/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {إن الإنسان لربه لكنود} [العاديات: 6] قال: " الكنود: الكفور، وقرأ: {إن الإنسان لكفور} [الحج: 66] "

TAB-FULL:v24p587/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p587/r3.speaker: أبو أمامة
TAB-FULL:v24p587/r3.claim: Abū Umāma says the ungrateful person lodges alone, beats his servant, and withholds hospitality.
TAB-FULL:v24p587/r3.anchor: عن أبي أمامة أنه كان يقول: " الكنود: الذي ينزل وحده، ويضرب عبده، ويمنع رفده "

TAB-FULL:v24p587/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p587/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p587/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the person blames his Lord, counting misfortunes and forgetting blessings.
TAB-FULL:v24p587/r4.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله {إن الإنسان لربه لكنود} [العاديات: 6] قال: «لوام لربه، يعد المصائب، وينسى النعم»

TABATABAI:100:6-11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r1.claim: Kanud means ungrateful; the verse parallels the description of humanity as ungrateful and portrays desire and worldly absorption as cutting people off from thanking God.
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r1.anchor: وهو إخبار عما في طبع الانسان من اتباع الهوى والانكباب على عرض الدنيا

TABATABAI:100:6-11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r2.claim: The passage hints that the raided people were ungrateful for Islam, God's greatest blessing, which brought good worldly life and eternal happiness.
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r2.anchor: وفيه تعريض للقوم المغار عليهم، وكأن المراد بكفرانهم كفرانهم بنعمة الإسلام التي أنعم الله بها عليهم وهي أعظم نعمة أوتوها

TABATABAI:100:6-11/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r10.speaker: مقاتل
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r10.claim: One account says the Prophet sent a company against a clan of Kinana led by al-Mundhir ibn Amr; when they were late, hypocrites assumed they had all been killed, and the sura revealed their horses' charge.
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r10.anchor: قيل بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم سرية إلى حي من كنانة فاستعمل عليهم المنذر بن عمرو الأنصاري أحد النقباء فتأخر رجوعهم

TABATABAI:100:6-11/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r11.claim: Another reported occasion says the sura came down after the Prophet sent Ali to Dhat al-Salasil, where he defeated the enemy after earlier companions had returned unsuccessful.
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r11.anchor: وقيل نزلت السورة لما بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عليا عليه السلام إلى ذات السلاسل فأوقع بهم وذلك

THALABI:v10p271/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p271/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والربيع
THALABI:v10p271/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Rabi interpret kanūd as ungrateful and denying God's blessings.
THALABI:v10p271/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والربيع: لكفور جحود لنعم الله تعالى

THALABI:v10p271/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p271/r2.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v10p271/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi gives regional meanings of kanūd: disobedient in Kindah, Hadramawt, and Maadd; ungrateful in Mudar, Rabiʿa, and Qudaʿa; miserly among Banu Malik.
THALABI:v10p271/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: هو بلسان كندة وحضرموت، وبلسان معد كلهم: العاصي

THALABI:v10p271/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p271/r3.speaker: سماك
THALABI:v10p271/r3.claim: Simak says the tribe Kinda was named because it cut off its father.
THALABI:v10p271/r3.anchor: وروى شعبة عن سماك أنه قال: إنما سميت كندة لأنها قطعت أباها

THALABI:v10p271/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p271/r4.speaker: ابن سيرين
THALABI:v10p271/r4.claim: Ibn Sirin interprets kanūd as one who reproaches his Lord.
THALABI:v10p271/r4.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين: هو اللوام لربه

THALABI:v10p271/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p271/r5.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p271/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says the kanūd counts calamities and forgets blessings; the cited poet likewise complains of misfortunes while forgetting favors.
THALABI:v10p271/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو الذي يعد المصائب وينسى النعم، أخذه الشاعر فقال:

WAHIDI-QT:100:6/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:100:6/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:100:6/r1.claim: The verse answers the oath: the human is ungrateful to his Lord, meaning the unbeliever denies God’s blessings.
WAHIDI-QT:100:6/r1.anchor: إن الإنسان } جواب القسم ،   { لربه لكنود } لكفور ،   يعني الكافر يجحد نعم الله تعالى

ASAD-NOTES:100:6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:100:6/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:100:6/r1.claim: Humanity is deeply ungrateful to God and bears witness to that ingratitude.
ASAD-NOTES:100:6/r1.anchor: VERILY, towards his Sustainer man is most ungrateful [3] (100:7) and to this, behold, he [himself] bears witness indeed

ASAD-NOTES:100:6#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:100:6#n3/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:100:6#n3/r1.claim: When people surrender to appetites symbolized by the charging horses, they forget God and their responsibility to Him.
ASAD-NOTES:100:6#n3/r1.anchor: whenever he surrenders to his appetites, symbolized by the madly storming chargers, he forgets God and his own responsibility to Him

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6:anmerkung/r1.claim: For kanud, consult WKAS under the root k-n-d; the implied ingratitude also appears in early Meccan 80:17.
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zum hier implizierten Gedanken der Undankbarkeit vgl. frühmekkanisch auch 80:17.

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r1.claim: An ʾinsan saying delays the eschatological resolution of the enigmatic oath opening; Neuwirth calls the saying a motif that later becomes a topos.
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die eschatologische Auflösung der enigmatischen Schwureinleitung wird durch einen – später zum Topos werdenden – ʾinsān-Spruch retardiert

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r2.claim: Verses 6–8 form the surah's structural center and contrast with the dynamic verbal and participial clauses around them; these are its only nominal sentences.
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r2.anchor: Sprachlich stehen V. 6–8, welche die strukturelle Mitte der Sure bilden, in deutlichem Kontrast zur dynamischen Aufgewühltheit von V. 1–5 und V. 9–11

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r3.claim: The passage accuses humanity of publicly bearing witness to ingratitude toward God in verses 6–7 and of possessiveness in verse 8.
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r3.anchor: Inhaltlich werden dem Menschen eine öffentlich „Bezeugung“ von Undank gegen Gott (V. 6–7) sowie Besitzgier (V. 8) vorgeworfen.

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r4.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r4.claim: Neuwirth reads these failings as examples of pre-Islamic anthropocentric values.
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r4.anchor: Neuwirth sieht hierin exemplarische Stellvertreter für den anthropozentrischen Wertekanon der vorislamischen Zeit

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r5.claim: The text does not explicitly criticize particular pre-Islamic Arab virtues.
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:6-8:kommentar/r5.anchor: doch kritisiert der Text nicht ausdrücklich bestimmte altarabische Tugenden.

ELMALILI:100:5-11/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r2.claim: Human beings, or some members of the species, are deeply ungrateful to their Lord and fail to acknowledge or thank Him for blessings.
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r2.anchor: Üzerindeki nimetinin hakkını tanımaz, şükrünü edâ etmez

ELMALILI:100:5-11/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r3.claim: The ungrateful person overlooks blessings, remembers hardships, and complains instead of doing his duty to God.
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r3.anchor: hep mâruz olduğu mesâib ve müşkilâtı anarak şikâyet ve itiraz eder durur

ELMALILI:100:5-11/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r4.claim: Kanūd is an emphatic form of kefūr, meaning intensely ungrateful; it can also mean one who persistently blames and denies blessings.
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r4.anchor: “Kenûd” “anûd” vezninde kefûr, yani çok küfrân-ı nimet edici demektir

ELMALILI:100:5-11/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r5.claim: The word can describe barren land, an ungrateful wife, a miser who eats alone, someone withholding a due gift, a stingy sinner, or a harsh master who beats servants.
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r5.anchor: Bir şey bitirmeyen verimsiz araziye ve kocasının hukūkuna iyiliklerine küfran eden nankör karıya

ELMALILI:100:5-11/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r6.speaker: çokları
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r6.claim: Most commentators take kanūd broadly of human nature as intense ingratitude for blessings.
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r6.anchor: Burada ekseriyetle tabî‘at-ı insâniyeye ait olmak üzere çokları

ELMALILI:100:5-11/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r7.speaker: Zeccâc
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses kanūd as disbeliever; the excerpt marks the citation with an editorial footnote.

ELMALILI:100:5-11/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r8.speaker: Hasan-ı Basrî
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r8.claim: Hasan al-Basri describes someone who recounts calamities, forgets blessings, and continually reproaches.
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r8.anchor: Hasan-ı Basrî mesâibi sayar, nimeti unutur levvâm demiş

ELMALILI:100:5-11/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r9.speaker: أبو أمامة
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r9.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits a Prophetic gloss from Abu Umama: the intensely ungrateful person eats alone, beats his servant, and withholds assistance.
ELMALILI:100:5-11/r9.anchor: İbn Cerîr Ebû Ümâme radıyallâhu anh’tan şöyle bir hadis de rivayet eylemiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r1.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r1.claim: Some read insan as humanity generally because these negative traits occur to some degree in everyone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r1.anchor: “insan” kavramıyla genel olarak insan türünün kastedildiği, çünkü bütün insanlarda bu tür olumsuz özelliklerin az çok bulunduğu belirtildiği gibi (bk. İbn Âşûr

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r2.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r2.claim: Another view is that insan especially means people who have not received guidance; Razi says this is the majority view.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r2.anchor: Râzî, bu ikinci yorumun çoğunluğun görüşü olduğunu belirtir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r4.speaker: hadis
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r4.claim: A hadith explains kanud as a person who eats alone, beats his enslaved person, and neglects financial obligations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:6/r4.anchor: bir hadiste şöyle açıklandığı rivayet edilir: “Öyle bir nankördür ki yalnız başına yer, kölesini döver, malî görevlerini yerine getirmez”

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p391/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p391/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p391/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله ﴿ لكنود ﴾ قال لكفور

ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r1.claim: Kanud means intensely ungrateful and rejecting blessings; a poem illustrates the term for one ungrateful to men's kindness.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r1.anchor: أى لكفور جحود من كند النعمة كفرها ولم يشكرها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil report dialectal glosses: Kinda and Hadramawt use it for a sinner, Rabiʿa and Mudar for an ingrate, and Kinana for a miser and poor master, like barren land; al-Kalbi gives a similar account with Malik for miser.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ومقاتل الكنود بلسان كندة وحضر موت العاصى وبلسان ربيعة ومضر الكفور

ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r3.claim: Most interpreters, including Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan, take it as ungrateful; a report from Abu Umama is attributed to the Prophet, and another report from al-Hasan describes blaming God, counting misfortunes, and forgetting blessings.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r3.anchor: والجمهور على تفسيره بالكفور وكل مما ذكر لايخلو عن كفران

ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r4.speaker: أبو أمامة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r4.claim: A weak Prophetic report from Abu Umama calls the ungrateful person one who beats a servant, withholds support, and eats alone; a parallel account is preserved as Abu Umama's own statement.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r4.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن أبى امامة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r5.claim: All reported meanings involve ingratitude, and extreme ingratitude gathers its different forms; “the human” is generic, but the judgment concerns some members of the class.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r5.anchor: والكفران المبلغ فيه يجمع صنوفا منه وال في الإنسان للجنس والحكم عليه بما ذكر باعتبار بعض الأفراد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r6.claim: Another view from Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about the specific unbeliever Qurt ibn Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Nawfal; the following warning might support this, but Alusi doubts the identification.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r6.anchor: وقيل المراد به كافر معين لما روى عن ابن عباس أنها نزلت في قرط بن عبد الله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r7.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r7.claim: Isam al-Din prefers a universal reading: human nature tends to ingratitude unless God protects a person; this also praises warriors who strive against their natural inclination.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد به كل الناس على معنى أن طبع الإنسان يجمله على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r8.claim: The prepositional phrase “to his Lord” attaches to “ungrateful”; its fronting serves the rhyme despite being especially relevant to the blame for denying God's favors.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p218/r8.anchor: ولربه متعلق بكنود واللام غير مانعة من ذلك وقدم للفاصلة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada say kanud means ungrateful, denying God's blessings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة: "لكنود": لكفور جحود لنعم الله تعالى.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r2.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says kanud means ungrateful in Mudar and Rabi'a dialect, but disobedient in Kinda and Hadramawt dialects.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: هو بلسان مضر وربيعة الكفور، وبلسان كندة وحضرموت العاصي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r3.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r3.claim: Hasan says the kanud person counts calamities and forgets blessings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو الذي يعد المصائب وينسى النعم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r4.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r4.claim: Ata says the kanud person does not give to others during hardship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r4.anchor: وقال عطاء: هو الذي لا يعطي في النائبة مع قومه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses kanud as having little good, like barren land that grows nothing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: هو قليل الخير، والأرض الكنود: التي لا تنبت شيئا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r6.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r6.claim: Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad says one offense makes the kanud forget many good deeds, while the grateful person forgets many wrongs because of one good deed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p509/r6.anchor: وقال الفضيل بن عياض: "الكنود" الذي أنسته الخصلة، الواحدة من الإساءة الخصال الكثيرة من الإحسان،

BAYDAWI-FULL:100:6-11/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:100:6-11/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:100:6-11/r1.claim: Kanūd means ungrateful for blessing, disobedient in Kinda's dialect, or miserly in Banū Mālik's dialect.
BAYDAWI-FULL:100:6-11/r1.anchor: لكفور من كند النعمة كنودا، أو لعاص بلغة كندة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r1.claim: Kanūd means intensely ungrateful and harsh in response to God, the benefactor who created, preserved, governed, and nurtured humanity; its intensive form describes one who scorns small favors and forgets many blessings over a little hardship.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r1.anchor: ومصدره الكنود بالضم وهو كفران النعمة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r2.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r2.claim: Al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ defines the ungrateful person as one bad experience making him forget many acts of kindness; gratitude is the opposite.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r2.anchor: هو من أنسته الخصلة الواحدة من الإساءةة الخصال الكثيرة من الإحسان

BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads the oath as emphasizing humanity’s ingratitude and miserliness with wealth, as if no one would be held accountable for how it was acquired or spent; he cites 99:7–8.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p510/r3.anchor: يبخل بما ليده من المال كأنه لا يجازي ولا يحاسب

DURR-FULL:v8p603/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r2.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r2.anchor: عن عطاء {والعاديات ضبحا} قال: الإبل {فالموريات قدحا} قال: الخيل {فوسطن به جمعا} قال: القوم {إن الإنسان لربه لكنود} قال: لكفور

DURR-FULL:v8p603/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb gives a pilgrimage reading: departure from ʿArafa, kindled fires, departure from Muzdalifa at dawn, the valley floor, and reaching Mina's Jamʿ.
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي {والعاديات ضبحا} قال: الدفعة من عرفة {فالموريات قدحا} قال: النيران تجمع {فالمغيرات صبحا}

DURR-FULL:v8p603/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r4.anchor: من طرق عن ابن عباس قال: الكنود بلساننا أهل البلد الكفور

DURR-FULL:v8p603/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r5.anchor: عن أبي أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله: {إن الإنسان لربه لكنود} قال: لكفور

DURR-FULL:v8p603/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r6.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r6.claim: The ungrateful person withholds support, lives alone, and beats his servant.
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r6.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال: الكنود الذي يمنع رفده وينزل وحده ويضرب عبده

DURR-FULL:v8p603/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r7.claim: In a report whose chain al-Suyuti calls weak, the Prophet describes the ungrateful as beating his servant, withholding support, and eating alone.
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r7.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن أبي أمامة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أتدرون ما الكنود

DURR-FULL:v8p603/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r8.speaker: قتادة والحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r8.claim: The ungrateful are thankless for blessings and miserly, withholding support, starving servants, eating alone, and not helping their community; all traits must be present.
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r8.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن في قوله: {إن الإنسان لربه لكنود} قال: الكفور للنعمة البخيل بما أعطى

DURR-FULL:v8p603/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r9.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r9.claim: The ungrateful count misfortunes and forget their Lord's blessings.
DURR-FULL:v8p603/r9.anchor: عن الحسن {إن الإنسان لربه لكنود} قال: لكفور يعدد المصيبات وينسى نعم ربه عز وجل

TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r7.claim: The intended sequence is that the human is ungrateful, intensely loves wealth, and God witnesses this; the witness clause is fronted as an intervening parenthesis.
TAB-FULL:v24p588#2/r7.anchor: وتأويل الكلام: إن الإنسان لربه لكنود، وإنه لحب الخير لشديد، وإن الله على ذلك من أمره لشاهد. ولكن قوله: {وإنه على ذلك لشهيد} [العاديات: 7] قدم

ASAD-NOTES:100:1#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:100:1#n2/r1.speaker: classical commentators
ASAD-NOTES:100:1#n2/r1.claim: The conventional reading treats the chargers as believers fighting jihad and therefore as laudable imagery.
ASAD-NOTES:100:1#n2/r1.anchor: believers' fight in God's cause (jihad) and, therefore, represent something highly commendable

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:9-11:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:9-11:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:9-11:kommentar/r2.claim: The sequence from accusation of wrongdoing to eschatological consequences also appears in Q104 in another literary form and recalls the basic form of Old Testament doom prophecy.
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:9-11:kommentar/r2.anchor: Die Sequenz aus einer Anklage menschlichen Fehlverhaltens (Q 100:6–8) und dem Aufweis der daraus folgenden eschatologischen Konsequenzen (Q 100:9–11) findet sich in anderer literarischer Gestalt auch in Q 104

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.claim: Riddling that creates rhetorical tension also structures oath sequences such as Q 100 and teaching questions at 90:12–16, 97:2–4, 101:1–11, and 104:5–9.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.anchor: auf dem Einsatz von Änigmatisierung zur Erzeugung rhetorischer Spannung basieren aber auch Schwurserien wie zu Beginn von Q 100

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r2.claim: The alternative that the word means warriors' horses is unsupported, especially because it leaves the oath unrelated to verse 6's assertion that man is ungrateful to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r2.anchor: What relationship can these words of the muqsam ‘alayh have with the horses of the warriors and the combatants?

TAB:100:6/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:6/r1.speaker: author
TAB:100:6/r1.claim: The human being is deeply ungrateful for the Lord's blessings.
TAB:100:6/r1.anchor: يقول :  إن الإنسان لكفور لنعم ربه

TAB:100:6/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:6/r2.speaker: author
TAB:100:6/r2.claim: In Arabic usage, barren land called kanūd grows nothing.
TAB:100:6/r2.anchor: والأرض الكنود :  التي لا تنبت شيئا

TAB:100:6/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:6/r3.speaker: author
TAB:100:6/r3.claim: Al-Aʿshā's poem uses kanud of something unresponsive to a visitor's repeated bond, illustrating the word's barren, unyielding sense.
TAB:100:6/r3.anchor: والأرض الكنود :  التي لا تنبت شيئا ،   قال الأعشى :  أحدث لها تحدث

TAB:100:6/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:6/r4.speaker: author
TAB:100:6/r4.claim: An etymology says the tribe Kinda was named because she severed her father.
TAB:100:6/r4.anchor: وقيل :  إنما سميت كندة :  لقطعها أباها

TAB:100:6/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:6/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:100:6/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses kanūd as ungrateful.
TAB:100:6/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قوله :  {  إنّ الإنسانَ لِرَبّهِ لَكَنُودٌ } قال :  لكفور

TAB:100:6/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:6/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:100:6/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد {  إن الإنسان لربه لكنود } قال :  لكفور

TAB:100:6/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:6/r7.speaker: الحسن البصري
TAB:100:6/r7.claim: Al-Hasan calls the person ungrateful: he counts his misfortunes and forgets his blessings.
TAB:100:6/r7.anchor: عن الحسن البصري :  {  إن الإنسان لربه لكنود } قال :  هو الكفور الذي يعد المصائب ،   وينسى نعم ربه

TAB:100:6/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:6/r8.speaker: الحسن
TAB:100:6/r8.claim: Al-Hasan also describes the person as reproaching his Lord by counting misfortunes.
TAB:100:6/r8.anchor: قال الحسن :  {  إن الإنسان لربه لكنود } يقول :  لوام لربه يعد المصائب

TAB:100:6/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:6/r10.speaker: قتادة
TAB:100:6/r10.anchor: عن قتادة {  إن الإنسان لربه لكنود } قال :  لكفور

TAB:100:6/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:6/r11.speaker: سماك
TAB:100:6/r11.claim: Simaak says the tribe Kinda was named because she severed her father.
TAB:100:6/r11.anchor: عن سماك أنه قال :  إنما سميت كندة :  أنها قطعت أباها

TAB:100:6/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:6/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:100:6/r12.claim: In a report from Abu Umama, the Prophet glosses kanūd as ungrateful and describes the person as eating alone, beating his servant, and withholding aid.
TAB:100:6/r12.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال :  قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB:100:6/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:6/r13.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:100:6/r13.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses kanūd as kafūr and cites the wording “indeed, the human is ungrateful.”

TAB:100:6/r14.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:6/r14.speaker: أبو أمامة
TAB:100:6/r14.claim: Abu Umama says kanūd describes one who lives alone, beats his servant, and withholds assistance.
TAB:100:6/r14.anchor: عن أبي أمامة أنه كان يقول :  الكنود :  الذي ينزل وحده ،   ويضرب عبده

ITQAN:v3p232#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r3.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abi al-Isba' identifies a rare pronoun shift: the passage starts by mentioning two subjects, turns from the human to report about his Lord, then returns to the human, a “shift of pronouns.”
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن أبي الاصبع جاء في القرآن من الالتفات قسم غريب جدا لم أظفر في الشعر بمثاله

ITQAN:v2p360/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p360/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p360/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains kanūd as ungrateful for blessings: a person who eats alone, withholds his help, and starves his servant; a cited poem uses the word for ingratitude.
ITQAN:v2p360/r8.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ لكنود ﴾ قال كفور للنعم وهو الذي يأكل وحده

ITQAN:v2p380/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p380/r17.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p380/r17.claim: In Kinana usage, kanūd means ungrateful for blessings.
ITQAN:v2p380/r17.anchor: 2480 ﴿ أسفارا ﴾ كتبا 2481 ﴿ أقتت ﴾ جمعت 2482 ﴿ لكنود ﴾ كفور للنعم

ITQAN:v4p537/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p537/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p537/r1.claim: A weak chain from Abu Umama attributes to the Prophet the explanation that kanud is one who eats alone, beats his servant, and withholds his support.
ITQAN:v4p537/r1.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ﴿ إن الإنسان لربه لكنود ﴾ قال ( الكنود الذي يأكل وحده ويضرب عبده ويمنع رفده )

DAMGHANI:v1p49/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r4.claim: In the description of the ungrateful human, al-insān refers to Qurāẓ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥubāb.
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r4.anchor: الرابع : الإنسان يعني قرظ بن عبد الله بن عمرو بن حباب . فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة العاديات

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r3.claim: They identify the ungrateful human in al-ʿĀdiyāt as Qarṭ ibn ʿAbd Allāh.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r3.anchor: والسادس : قرط بن عبد الله ومنه قوله

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r2.claim: The reported exchange glosses kanūd as kafūr; Bint al-Shati then cites Arabic poetry to establish that the word was known.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r2.anchor: ما الكنود؟ قال: الكفور. قال: وهل كانت العرب تعرف ذلك؟ قال: نعم، أما سمعت بقول أبي زُبَيْد الطائي

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r3.claim: A variant gloss defines kanūd as ungrateful for blessings, eating alone, withholding food from a guest, and starving a servant.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r3.anchor: وفي (تق) كنود للنعم، وهو الذي يأكل وحده ويمنع لافده. زاد في (ك، ط) : ويجيع عبده

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r4.speaker: أبو زبيد الطائي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r4.claim: Abu Zubayd's line uses kanūd of a miserly age as Arabic evidence for the word's sense of ingratitude.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r4.anchor: بقول أبي زبيد الطائي: إنْ تَفُتْنى [فلم] أطِبْ عنك نفساً. . . غيرَ أني أمَتَّى بدَهرٍ كُنَود

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r5.speaker: الشاعر
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r5.claim: A second poetic witness describes the speaker as not kanūd toward a benefactor's generosity.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p436/r5.anchor: وشاهده في الثلاثة، قول الشاعر: شكرتُ له يومَ العكاظِ نوالهَ. . . ولم أكُ للمعروفِ ثَمَّ كَنُودا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r1.speaker: الكلبي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says kanūd means ungrateful for blessings in the dialect of Kinda and Hadramawt; al-Farra transmits this gloss.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي، وزعم أنها لغة في كندة وحضرموت: لكنود: لكفور بالنعمة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r2.speaker: الحسن
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r2.claim: Al-Hasan glosses kanūd as one who reproaches his Lord over misdeeds while forgetting blessings.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: لوام لربه المسيئات وينسى النعم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r3.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r3.claim: A report from the Prophet through Abū Umāma calls the kanūd one who eats alone, withholds his help, and beats his servant; no grading is given.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r3.anchor: ورووا فيه حديث أبي أمامة الباهلي عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: قال: (الكنود هو الذي يأكل وحده ويمنع رفده ويضرب عبده)

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r4.claim: A second report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās in a marfūʿ form describes the kanūd as one who lives alone, withholds assistance, and whips his servant.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس مرفوعاً بلفظ: (من نزل وحده ومنع رفده وجَلَد عبده)

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives dialectal glosses: rebel in Kinda and Hadramawt, ungrateful in Rabīʿa and Muḍar, and miserly or a bad master in Kināna.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا أنه قال: الكنود بلسان كندة وحضرموت: العاصي، وبلسان ربيعة ومضر: الكفور

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r6.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r6.claim: Al-Rāghib defines kanūd as ingratitude for God’s blessing.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r6.anchor: وفي (مفردات الراغب) أنه الكفران بنعمة الله.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r7.claim: Bint al-Shati traces kanūd to barren, resistant earth that refuses crops: hence the sense of being stingy and withholding a blessing’s due, close to denying kindness.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r7.anchor: والأرجح أنها ترجع إلى الأرض الكنود: تعصي على الزرع فلا تنبت، فهي عاصية وبخيلة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r8.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r8.claim: Although the reported glosses are close, the best fit in al-ʿĀdiyāt is denial and ingratitude toward God’s blessings.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p437/r8.anchor: وأقرب معانيها إلى آية العاديات، أنه الجحود والكفران بنعمته تعالى، والله أعلم.

ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r1.claim: Kanūd means ungrateful for a blessing.

ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r2.claim: A cited poet uses kanūd for someone ungrateful for people’s favors.
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r2.anchor: قال الشاعر : كنود لنعماء الرجال ومن يكن *** كنوداً لنعماء الرجال يبعد

ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives regional senses: disobedient in Kinda and Hadramawt, ungrateful in Rabīʿa and Muḍar, and miserly with a bad disposition in Kināna.
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : الكنود ،   بلسان كندة وحضرموت : العاصي ؛ وبلسان ربيعة ومضر : الكفور ؛ وبلسان كنانة : البخيل السيئ الملكة ،   وقاله مقاتل

ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r4.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r4.claim: Muqātil agrees with Ibn ʿAbbās’s dialect glosses.
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : الكنود ،   بلسان كندة وحضرموت : العاصي ؛ وبلسان ربيعة ومضر : الكفور ؛ وبلسان كنانة : البخيل السيئ الملكة ،   وقاله مقاتل

ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r5.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī gives a similar account but says Banū Mālik use kanūd for a miser and omits Hadramawt.
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r5.anchor: وقال الكلبي مثله إلا أنه قال : وبلسان بني مالك : البخيل ،   ولم يذكر وحضرموت

ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r6.claim: The expression kand al-niʿma means to be ungrateful for a blessing.
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r6.anchor: ويقال : كند النعمة كنوداً . وقال أبو زبيد

ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r7.speaker: أبو زبيد
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r7.claim: Abū Zubayd’s verse about a miser illustrates kanūd as stinginess.
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r7.anchor: وقال أبو زبيد في البخيل : إن تفتني فلم أطب عنك نفسا *** غير أني أمنى بدهر كنود

ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r8.claim: The oath’s object is the genus of charging horses, with al- not referring to a previously specified group; the sworn assertion is that humans are ungrateful to their Lord.
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن المقسم به هو جنس العاديات ،   وليست أل فيه للعهد ،   والمقسم عليه : { إن الإنسان لربه لكنود }

ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r9.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r9.claim: A hadith describes the kanūd as eating alone, withholding his support, and striking his servant.
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r9.anchor: وفي الحديث : « الكنود يأكل وحده ويمنع رفده ويضرب عبده »

ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan gloss kanūd as denying God’s blessing.
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن : هو الجحود لنعمة الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r11.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan also says the kanūd blames his Lord, counts misfortunes, and forgets blessings.
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r11.anchor: وعن الحسن أيضاً : هو اللائم لربه ،   يعد السيئات وينسى الحسنات

ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r12.speaker: الفضيل
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r12.claim: Al-Fuḍayl describes someone whose one sin makes him forget many good deeds and who treats God as if worship were a transaction.
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r12.anchor: وقال الفضيل : هو الذي تنسيه سيئة واحدة حسنات كثيرة ،   ويعامل الله على عقد عوض

ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r13.speaker: عطاء
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r13.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the kanūd does not support his people in times of calamity.
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r13.anchor: وقال عطاء : هو الذي لا يغطى في النائبات مع قومه

ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r14.claim: Another gloss identifies kanūd simply as a miser.

ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r15.speaker: ابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r15.claim: Ibn Qutayba says an arḍ kanūd is land that grows nothing.
ABUHAYYAN:100:6/r15.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة : أرض كنود : لا تنبت شيئاً

ALUSI:100:6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:100:6/r1.claim: Kanūd means ungrateful and unthankful, from k-n-d, to deny a favor rather than give thanks; the cited couplet uses the word for an ungrateful person.
ALUSI:100:6/r1.anchor: أي لكفور جحود من كند النعمة كفرها ولم يشكرها وأنشدوا

ALUSI:100:6/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
ALUSI:100:6/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil give dialect senses: in Kinda and Ḥaḍramawt, disobedient; in Rabīʿa and Muḍar, ungrateful; in Kināna, miserly and badly managed, like barren land.
ALUSI:100:6/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ومقاتل الكنود بلسان كندة وحضرموت العاصي وبلسان ربيعة ومضر الكفور

ALUSI:100:6/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:6/r3.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI:100:6/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī gives a similar dialect gloss, but says Banu Mālik use kanūd for miserly and omits Ḥaḍramawt.
ALUSI:100:6/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي نحوه إلا أنه قال وبلسان بني مالك البخيل ولم يذكر حضرموت

ALUSI:100:6/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:6/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
ALUSI:100:6/r4.claim: The interpretation of kanūd as ungrateful is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan; Ibn ʿAsākir also transmits it from Abū Umāma as a Prophetic report.
ALUSI:100:6/r4.anchor: وتفسيره بالكفور هنا مروى عن ابن عباس والحسن وأخرجه ابن عساكر عن أبي أمامة مرفوعاً

ALUSI:100:6/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:6/r5.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI:100:6/r5.claim: Another report from al-Ḥasan defines the person as one who complains against his Lord, counts his misfortunes, and forgets his blessings.
ALUSI:100:6/r5.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عن الحسن أنه قال هو اللائم لربه عز وجل يعد السيآت وينسى الحسنات

ALUSI:100:6/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:6/r6.speaker: أبو أمامة
ALUSI:100:6/r6.claim: A weak-chain report from Abū Umāma quotes the Prophet defining kanūd as one who beats his servant, withholds his provision, and eats alone.
ALUSI:100:6/r6.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن أبي أمامة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI:100:6/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:6/r7.speaker: أبو أمامة
ALUSI:100:6/r7.claim: Al-Bukhārī's al-Adab al-Mufrad, al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī, and others transmit mawqūf from Abū Umāma the gloss: one who withholds provision, eats alone, and beats his servant.
ALUSI:100:6/r7.anchor: وأخرج البخاري في الأدب المفرد والحكيم الترمذي وغيرهما تفسيره بالذي يمنع رفده

ALUSI:100:6/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:6/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:100:6/r8.claim: The majority prefer ungrateful; each reported trait entails ingratitude, and extreme ingratitude gathers its many forms.
ALUSI:100:6/r8.anchor: والجمهور على تفسيره بالكفور وكل مما ذكر لا يخلو عن كفران

ALUSI:100:6/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:6/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:100:6/r9.claim: Al-insān is generic, but the judgment applies only to some individuals.
ALUSI:100:6/r9.anchor: وأل في الإنسان للجنس والحكم عليه بما ذكر باعتبار بعض الأفراد

ALUSI:100:6/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:6/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:100:6/r10.claim: A view attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās identifies a specific disbeliever, Qurṭ b. ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr b. Nawfal, based on the following verse; al-Ālūsī questions both the specific identification and its argument.
ALUSI:100:6/r10.anchor: وقيل المراد به كافر معين لما روي عن ابن عباس أنها نزلت في قرط بن عبد الله

ALUSI:100:6/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:6/r11.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:100:6/r11.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn prefers that humanity is meant: human nature inclines to ingratitude unless God protects a person, which also praises warriors for acting against their nature.
ALUSI:100:6/r11.anchor: وقيل المراد به كل الناس على معنى أن طبع الإنسان يحمله على ذلك إلا إذا عصمه الله

ALUSI:100:6/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:6/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:100:6/r12.claim: Li-rabbihi remains attached to kanūd despite the intervening lām; it is fronted for the verse ending and because ingratitude for God's favor is especially blameworthy.
ALUSI:100:6/r12.anchor: ولربه متعلق بكنود واللام غير مانعة من ذلك وقدم للفاصلة

ALUSI:100:6/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:100:6/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:100:6/r13.claim: Another explanation says li-rabbihi is fronted for emphatic restriction.

BAGHAWI:100:6/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:100:6/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة
BAGHAWI:100:6/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada explain kanūd as ungrateful and denying God’s blessings.
BAGHAWI:100:6/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس ، ومجاهد ، وقتادة : { لكنود } لكفور جحود لنعم الله تعالى

BAGHAWI:100:6/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:100:6/r2.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI:100:6/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says kanūd means ungrateful in the speech of Mudar and Rabiʿa, but sinner in Kinda and Hadramawt.
BAGHAWI:100:6/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي : هو بلسان مضر وربيعة : الكفور ، وبلسان كندة وحضرموت : العاصي

BAGHAWI:100:6/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:100:6/r3.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI:100:6/r3.claim: Al-Hasan calls kanūd the person who counts misfortunes and forgets blessings.
BAGHAWI:100:6/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن : هو الذي يعد المصائب ، وينسى النعم

BAGHAWI:100:6/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:100:6/r4.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI:100:6/r4.claim: ʿAta says kanūd is one who does not give to his people when hardship strikes.
BAGHAWI:100:6/r4.anchor: وقال عطاء : هو الذي لا يعطي في النائبة مع قومه

BAGHAWI:100:6/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:100:6/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI:100:6/r5.claim: Abu ʿUbayda explains kanūd as having little good, like barren land that grows nothing.
BAGHAWI:100:6/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : هو قليل الخير ، والأرض الكنود : التي لا تنبت شيئاً

BAGHAWI:100:6/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:100:6/r6.speaker: الفضيل ابن عياض
BAGHAWI:100:6/r6.claim: Al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyad contrasts the thankless person, whose one offense eclipses many favors, with the grateful person, whose one favor eclipses many offenses.
BAGHAWI:100:6/r6.anchor: وقال الفضيل ابن عياض : الكنود الذي أنسته الخصلة الواحدة من الإساءة الخصال الكثيرة من الإحسان

BAYDAWI:100:6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:100:6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:100:6/r1.claim: Kanūd means ungrateful for blessings, disobedient in the language of Kinda, or stingy in the language of Banū Mālik.
BAYDAWI:100:6/r1.anchor: { إن الإنسان لربه لكنود } لكفور ، من كند النعمة كنودا ، أو العاص بلغة كندة ، أو لبخيل بلغة بني مالك

BAYDAWI:100:6/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:100:6/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:100:6/r2.claim: The statement is the answer to the oath.
BAYDAWI:100:6/r2.anchor: أو لبخيل بلغة بني مالك ، وهو جواب القسم

BIQAI:100:6/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:6/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:6/r1.claim: The oath pairs noble horses with humanity, the highest creature distinguished by speech; human thoughts gallop like racehorses.
BIQAI:100:6/r1.anchor: ولما أقسم بالخيل التي هي أشرف الحيوان ، كما أن الإنسان المقسم لأجله أشرف ما اتصف منه بالبيان ، وتجري به أفكاره كخيل الرهان

BIQAI:100:6/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:6/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:6/r2.claim: The mind's meanings may sparkle with noble truth or be joined to falsehood, slander, heresy, and rebellion.
BIQAI:100:6/r2.anchor: وتقدح المعاني تارة مقترنة بأشرف اللمعان ، وأخرى بأخس ما يقع به الاقتران ، من الزور والبهتان ، والإلحاد والطغيان

BIQAI:100:6/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:6/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:6/r3.claim: Raiding usually seeks unjust seizure of property; even in jihad, few fighters act sincerely for God alone.
BIQAI:100:6/r3.anchor: وكانت الإغارة في الغالب لأجل قهر المغار عليهم على أموالهم عدواناً إن كان ذلك في غير الجهاد ، وإن كانت في الجهاد فقل من يخلص

BIQAI:100:6/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:6/r4.speaker: حديث قدسي
BIQAI:100:6/r4.claim: A qudsi hadith says God's wholly devoted servant is the one who remembers Him when facing his peer or opponent; no grading is stated.
BIQAI:100:6/r4.anchor: كما أشار إليه الحديث القدسي : " إن عبدي كل عبدي للذي يذكرني عند لقاء قرنه "

BIQAI:100:6/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:6/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:6/r5.claim: The oath's answer judges humanity as a kind; the rare sincere person is treated as nonexistent, and the emphatic assertion counters people's denial of this condition.
BIQAI:100:6/r5.anchor: قال مجيباً للقسم بذكر المقسم عليه حاكماً على النوع باعتبار عد المخلص لقلته عدماً ، مؤكداً لما لهم من تكذيب ذلك

BIQAI:100:6/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:6/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:6/r6.claim: Al-insān means the human species, characterized here by familiarity with itself and forgetfulness of what benefits it.
BIQAI:100:6/r6.anchor: { إن الإنسان } أي هذا النوع بما له من الأنس بنفسه ، والنسيان لما ينفعه

BIQAI:100:6/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:6/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:6/r7.claim: His Lord is the benefactor who brought him into being, sustains him, governs him, and nurtures him.
BIQAI:100:6/r7.anchor: { لربه } أي المحسن إليه بإبداعه ، ثم إبقائه وتدبيره وتربيته

BIQAI:100:6/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:6/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:6/r8.claim: The ungrateful person turns God's gifts of fine horses and mental and bodily strength toward what He forbade.
BIQAI:100:6/r8.anchor: حيث يقدم بما أحسن به الله إليه من الصافنات الجياد ، وبما آتاه من قوة الجنان والأركان على ما نهاه عنه

BIQAI:100:6/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:6/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:6/r9.claim: Kanūd derives from al-kanūd, with ḍamma, meaning ingratitude for blessings.
BIQAI:100:6/r9.anchor: ومصدره الكنود بالضم وهو كفران النعمة

BIQAI:100:6/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:6/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI:100:6/r10.claim: The emphatic form describes someone who dismisses small gifts, fails to thank for much, forgets abundant blessings after slight hardship, and complains of the least affliction.
BIQAI:100:6/r10.anchor: من يزدري القليل ولا يشكر الكثير ، وينسى كثير النعمة بقليل المحنة

BIQAI:100:6/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:6/r11.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
BIQAI:100:6/r11.claim: Al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ says one misdeed can make a person forget many acts of kindness; the grateful person is the opposite.
BIQAI:100:6/r11.anchor: وقال الفضيل بن عياض : هو من أنسته الخصلة الواحدة من الإساءة الخصال الكثيرة من الإحسان ، والشكور ضده

BIQAI:100:6/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:100:6/r12.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:100:6/r12.claim: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr glosses kanūd as ingratitude and miserliness with wealth, as if no reckoning asked how it was earned or spent; he links this to 99:7–8.
BIQAI:100:6/r12.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير : أقسم سبحانه على حال الإنسان بما هو ، فقال : " إن الإنسان لربه لكنود " أي لكفور ، يبخل بما لديه من المال

DURR:100:6/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:100:6/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:100:6/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says kanūd in the local dialect means an ingrate or ungrateful person.
DURR:100:6/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : الكنود بلساننا -أهل البلد - الكفور .

DURR:100:6/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:100:6/r2.speaker: النبي
DURR:100:6/r2.claim: A report from Abū Umāma attributes to the Prophet the gloss that kanūd means “very ungrateful.”
