DURR:100:6/r2.anchor: عن أبي أمامة ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله : { إن الإنسان لربه لكنود } قال : لكفور .

DURR:100:6/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:100:6/r3.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR:100:6/r3.claim: Abū Umāma describes the kanūd as one who withholds his hospitality, lives alone, and beats his servant.
DURR:100:6/r3.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال : الكنود : الذي يمنع رفده ، وينزل وحده ، ويضرب عبده .

DURR:100:6/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:100:6/r4.speaker: النبي
DURR:100:6/r4.claim: In a chain explicitly called weak, Abū Umāma reports the Prophet defining kanūd as an ingrate who beats his servant, withholds generosity, and eats alone.
DURR:100:6/r4.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «أتدرون ما الكنود ؟

DURR:100:6/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:100:6/r5.speaker: قتادة والحسن
DURR:100:6/r5.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḥasan say kanūd combines ingratitude for blessings, miserliness, withholding help, starving one’s servant, eating alone, and failing to aid one’s community; all traits must occur together.
DURR:100:6/r5.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن في قوله : { إن الإنسان لربه لكنود } قال

DURR:100:6/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:100:6/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR:100:6/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses kanūd as ungrateful: a person counts misfortunes while forgetting the blessings of his Lord.
DURR:100:6/r6.anchor: عن الحسن { إن الإنسان لربه لكنود } قال : لكفور ، يعدد المصيبات ، وينسى نعم ربه عز وجل

IBNASHUR:100:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:100:6/r1.claim: This sentence is the response to the sūra's preceding oath.
IBNASHUR:100:6/r1.anchor: وجملة :  { إن الإنسان لربه لكنود } جواب القسم .

IBNASHUR:100:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:6/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:100:6/r2.claim: Kanūd is an intensive adjective: in Muḍar and Rabīʿa it means ungrateful for blessings, in Kināna miserly, and in Kinda and Ḥaḍramawt disobedient; here it means intensely ungrateful to God.
IBNASHUR:100:6/r2.anchor: والكنود :  وصف من أمثلة المبالغة من كند ولغات العرب مختلفة في معناه فهو في لغة مضر وربيعةَ :  الكفور بالنعمة

IBNASHUR:100:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:100:6/r3.claim: Al-insān is generic and usually exhaustive: human beings are disposed to ingratitude, except prophets and the most complete righteous, because self-preference is innate and only vigilance and remembering others' rights restrain it.
IBNASHUR:100:6/r3.anchor: والتعريف في { الإنسان } تعريف الجنس وهو يفيد الاستغراق غالباً ،  أي أن في طبع الإنسان الكنود لربه

IBNASHUR:100:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:6/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:100:6/r4.claim: People may forget or neglect God's due while pursuing their own desires; their ability to resist this ingrained trait varies, and it appears in shirk, disobedience, or failure to use blessings for their intended purpose.
IBNASHUR:100:6/r4.anchor: وبذلك قد يذهل أو ينسى حق الله ،  والإنسان يحس بذلك من نفسه في خطراته ،  ويتوانى أو يغفل عن مقاومته

IBNASHUR:100:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:6/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:100:6/r5.claim: Shirk, disobedience, and failing to use a blessing for its intended purpose are all degrees of ingratitude, so God warns people to discipline this ingrained trait.
IBNASHUR:100:6/r5.anchor: فالإشراك كنود ،  والعصيان كنود ،  وقلة ملاحظة صرف النعمة فيما أعطيت لأجله كنود ،  وهو متفاوت

IBNASHUR:100:6/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:6/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:100:6/r6.claim: Other Qurʾānic descriptions of human dispositions reinforce this warning: humans are created anxious and hasty, and the transgression when self-sufficient was discussed earlier.
IBNASHUR:100:6/r6.anchor: كما في قوله تعالى :  { إن الإنسان خلق هلوعاً }  [ المعارج :  19 ] وقوله :  { خلق الإنسان من عجل }

IBNASHUR:100:6/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:6/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR:100:6/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes al-insān here specifically as the disbeliever, an instance of conventional generic usage.
IBNASHUR:100:6/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس :  تخصيص الإنسان هنا بالكافر فهو من العموم العرفي .

IBNASHUR:100:6/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:6/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR:100:6/r8.claim: Abū Umāma al-Bāhilī reports a weakly transmitted Prophetic definition of the kanūd as one who eats alone, withholds support, and beats his servant.
IBNASHUR:100:6/r8.anchor: وروي عن أبي أمامة الباهلي بسند ضعيف قال :  قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم « الكنود هو الذي يأكل وحده ويمنع رفده

IBNASHUR:100:6/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:6/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:100:6/r9.claim: The reported acts illustrate lesser degrees of ingratitude: not feeding others, withholding aid, or beating a servant forgets God's favor; more serious forms are all the more aptly called kanūd.
IBNASHUR:100:6/r9.anchor: وهو تفسير لأدنى معاني الكنود فإن أكله وحده ،  أي عدم إطعامه أحداً معه ،  أو عدم إطعامه المحاويج

IBNASHUR:100:6/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:6/r10.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR:100:6/r10.claim: One reported view takes al-insān as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra rather than humanity generically.
IBNASHUR:100:6/r10.anchor: وقيل التعريف في { الإنسان } للعهد ،  وأن المراد به الوليد بن المغيرة

IBNASHUR:100:6/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:6/r11.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR:100:6/r11.claim: Another reported view identifies al-insān as Qurṭah ibn ʿAbd ʿAmr ibn Nawfal al-Qurashī.
IBNASHUR:100:6/r11.anchor: وقيل :  قرطة بن عبد عمرو بن نوفل القرشي

IBNASHUR:100:6/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:6/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:100:6/r12.claim: The lām before rabbihi strengthens the object relation: kanūd is a derived adjective rather than an inherently transitive verb, yet commonly takes its object with lām, here after the predicate.
IBNASHUR:100:6/r12.anchor: واللام في { لربه } لام التقوية لأن ( كنود ) وصف ليس أصيلاً في العمل ،  وإنما يتعلق بالمعمولات لمشابهته الفعل في الاشتقاق

IBNASHUR:100:6/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:6/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:100:6/r13.claim: Fronting li-rabbihi spotlights the outrageous object of ingratitude—God, most deserving of thanks—and the lām of the predicate adds emphatic astonishment.
IBNASHUR:100:6/r13.anchor: وتقديم { لربه } لإفادة الاهتمام بمتعلق هذا الكنود لتشنيع هذا الكنود بأنه كنود للرب الذي هو أحق الموجودات بالشكر

IBNASHUR:100:6/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:100:6/r14.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNASHUR:100:6/r14.claim: Ibn Hishām holds that the lām of inna's predicate is not a particle requiring initial position, explaining how the genitive li-rabbihi can precede it.
IBNASHUR:100:6/r14.anchor: وابن هشام يرى أن لام الابتداء الواقعة في خبر ( إنَّ ) ليست بذات صدارة

IBNATIYYA:100:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r1.claim: The oath's answer is the statement that the human is ungrateful to his Lord.
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r1.anchor: والقسم واقع على قوله : { إن الإنسان لربه لكنود }

IBNATIYYA:100:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r2.claim: A report attributes to the Prophet the definition of kanud as an ingrate who eats alone, withholds his help, and beats his servant.
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r2.anchor: وروي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : «أتدرون ما الكنود ؟ »

IBNATIYYA:100:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r3.claim: Kanud can describe believers who are ungrateful for blessings; the sense is ungrateful for the Lord's blessing.
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r3.anchor: وقد يكون من المؤمنين الكفور بالنعمة ، فتقدير الآية : إن الإنسان لنعمة ربه لكنود

IBNATIYYA:100:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r4.claim: A barren land that grows nothing is called kanūd.

IBNATIYYA:100:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says kanud is one who blames his Lord, counting misfortunes while forgetting blessings.
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن : الكنود : اللائم لربه

IBNATIYYA:100:6/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r6.claim: In the dialect of Kinda, kanud means disobedient; horses are also called kanud.
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r6.anchor: والكنود : العاصي بلغة كندة ، ويقال للخيل : كنود

IBNATIYYA:100:6/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r7.claim: Abu Zubayd's verse uses kanud for a miserly, withholding era that denies a person what he wants.

IBNATIYYA:100:6/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r8.speaker: الفضيل
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r8.claim: Al-Fudayl says the kanud lets one bad deed make him forget many good deeds and treats God as if under a contract of compensation.
IBNATIYYA:100:6/r8.anchor: وقال الفضيل : الكنود الذي تنسيه سيئة واحدة حسنات كثيرة

IBNKATHIR:100:6/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:100:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:100:6/r1.claim: This statement is the object of the preceding oath: humanity is ungrateful and denies its Lord's blessings.
IBNKATHIR:100:6/r1.anchor: هذا هو المقسم عليه ، بمعنى أنه لنعم ربه لجحود كفور

IBNKATHIR:100:6/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:100:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وإبراهيم النخعي، وأبو الجوزاء، وأبو العالية، وأبو الضحى، وسعيد بن جبير، ومحمد بن قيس، والضحاك، والحسن، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس، وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR:100:6/r2.claim: These authorities gloss kanūd as intensely ungrateful or disbelieving toward God's blessings.
IBNKATHIR:100:6/r2.anchor: الربيع بن أنس ، وابن زيد : الكنود : الكفور

IBNKATHIR:100:6/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:100:6/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR:100:6/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says the ungrateful person keeps count of misfortunes and forgets his Lord's blessings.
IBNKATHIR:100:6/r3.anchor: قال الحسن : هو الذي يعد المصائب ، وينسى نعم ربه

IBNKATHIR:100:6/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:100:6/r4.speaker: أبو أمامة
IBNKATHIR:100:6/r4.claim: A report from Abu Umamah calls the kanūd person ungrateful, eating alone, beating his servant, and withholding help; Ibn Kathir calls its marfuʿ chain weak because Jaʿfar b. al-Zubayr is abandoned, and notes al-Tabari's mawquf version.
IBNKATHIR:100:6/r4.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI:100:6/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:6/r1.speaker: قتادة، والضحاك، وابن جبير
MAWARDI:100:6/r1.claim: Qatada, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Jubayr gloss kanud as ungrateful or unbelieving; the word can describe one who disbelieves in little and fails to thank for much.
MAWARDI:100:6/r1.anchor: أحدها : لكفور ، قاله قتادة ، والضحاك ، وابن جبير ،

MAWARDI:100:6/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:6/r2.speaker: الأعشى
MAWARDI:100:6/r2.claim: Al-Aʿsha's line calls a person kanud for failing to reciprocate the visitor's customary bond, illustrating ingratitude.
MAWARDI:100:6/r2.anchor: ومنه قول الأعشى : أَحْدِثْ لها تحدث لوصْلك ، إنها *** كُنَدٌ لوصْلِ الزائرِ المُعْتادِ

MAWARDI:100:6/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:6/r3.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI:100:6/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says kanud is one who complains to his Lord, recalling calamities while forgetting blessings; this is close to the first sense.
MAWARDI:100:6/r3.anchor: الثاني : أنه اللوام لربه ، يذكر المصائب ، وينسى النعم ، قاله الحسن ، وهو قريب من المعنى الأول .

MAWARDI:100:6/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:6/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:100:6/r4.claim: Another gloss is one who denies the truth; an etymological explanation says Kinda was named for denying its father.
MAWARDI:100:6/r4.anchor: الثالث : أن الكنود الجاحد للحق ، وقيل : إنما سميت كندة لأنها جحدت أباها

MAWARDI:100:6/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:6/r5.speaker: إبراهيم بن زهير
MAWARDI:100:6/r5.claim: Ibrahim b. Zuhayr's line uses kanud for a miserly woman who is proud and turns away.
MAWARDI:100:6/r5.anchor: وقال إبراهيم بن زهير الشاعر : دع البخلاء إن شمخوا وصدوا *** وذكرى بخل غانية كنود

MAWARDI:100:6/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:6/r6.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI:100:6/r6.claim: Yahya b. Sallam says kanud means disobedient in the dialects of Kinda and Hadramawt.
MAWARDI:100:6/r6.anchor: الرابع : أن الكنود العاصي بلسان كندة وحضرموت ، وذكره يحيى بن سلام .

MAWARDI:100:6/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:6/r7.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI:100:6/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi distinguishes dialects: kanud means disobedient in Kinda and Hadramawt, ungrateful among Mudar and Rabiʿa, and miserly among Malik b. Kinana.
MAWARDI:100:6/r7.anchor: وقال الكلبي : الكنود بلسان كندة وحضرموت : العاصي ، وبلسان مضر وربيعة : الكفور

MAWARDI:100:6/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:6/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI:100:6/r8.claim: A fifth gloss is that kanud means miserly in the dialect of Malik b. Kinana.
MAWARDI:100:6/r8.anchor: الخامس : أنه البخيل بلسان مالك بن كنانة

MAWARDI:100:6/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:6/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI:100:6/r9.claim: A further possibility is that the person spends God's blessings in acts of disobedience to God.
MAWARDI:100:6/r9.anchor: السادس : أنه ينفق نعم الله في معاصي الله .

MAWARDI:100:6/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:6/r10.speaker: النبي
MAWARDI:100:6/r10.claim: Al-Qasim reports through Abu Umama that the Prophet describes the kanud as one who hits his servant, eats alone, and withholds his support.
MAWARDI:100:6/r10.anchor: السابع : ما رواه القاسم عن أبي أمامة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " الكنود الذي يضرب عبده ، ويأكل وحده ، ويمنع رفده "

MAWARDI:100:6/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:6/r11.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:100:6/r11.claim: Al-Dahhak says this verse was revealed about al-Walid b. al-Mughira.
MAWARDI:100:6/r11.anchor: وقال الضحاك : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة .

MAWARDI:100:6/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:100:6/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI:100:6/r12.claim: On this interpretation, the oath is sworn by all the things previously mentioned in the sura.
MAWARDI:100:6/r12.anchor: وعلى هذا وقع القسم بجميع ما تقدم من السورة .

NASAFI:100:6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:100:6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:100:6/r1.claim: Kanūd means intensely ungrateful, particularly for his Lord's blessings.
NASAFI:100:6/r1.anchor: وجواب القسم { إن الإنسان لربه لكنود } لكفور

QURTUBI:100:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:100:6/r1.claim: This is the answer to the oath: people are disposed to be ungrateful for blessings.
QURTUBI:100:6/r1.anchor: هذا جواب لنعم القسم ،   أي طبع الإنسان على كفران النعمة

QURTUBI:100:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:100:6/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines kanūd as very ungrateful and denying God’s blessings.
QURTUBI:100:6/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : " لكنود " لكفور جحود لنعم الله

QURTUBI:100:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r3.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI:100:6/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the kanūd recalls calamities and forgets blessings; a poet restates this contrast.
QURTUBI:100:6/r3.anchor: وكذلك قال الحسن .   وقال : يذكر المصائب ،   وينسى النعم

QURTUBI:100:6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r4.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI:100:6/r4.claim: The poem illustrates ingratitude as complaining of calamities while forgetting blessings.
QURTUBI:100:6/r4.anchor: إلى متى أنت وحَتَّى مَتَى *** تشكو المصيباتِ وتنسى النعم

QURTUBI:100:6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r5.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي
QURTUBI:100:6/r5.claim: The Prophet defines the kanūd as one who eats alone, withholds his gifts, and beats his servant; al-Tirmidhī al-Ḥakīm transmits it in Nawādir al-Uṣūl without a grading stated here.
QURTUBI:100:6/r5.anchor: الكنود ،   هو الذي يأكل وحده ،   ويمنع رفده

QURTUBI:100:6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:100:6/r6.claim: Another Prophetic report calls the worst person one who lives alone, withholds his gift, and lashes his servant; al-Tirmidhī al-Ḥakīm transmits it in Nawādir al-Uṣūl.
QURTUBI:100:6/r6.anchor: من نزل وحده ،   ومنع رفده ،   وجلد عبده

QURTUBI:100:6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:100:6/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says kanūd means disobedient in Kinda and Ḥaḍramawt dialects.
QURTUBI:100:6/r7.anchor: وقد روي عن عباس أيضا أنه قال : الكنود بلسان كندة وحضر موت : العاصي

QURTUBI:100:6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:100:6/r8.claim: In the dialects of Rabīʿa and Muḍar, Ibn ʿAbbās says kanūd means unbelieving or ungrateful.

QURTUBI:100:6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r9.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
QURTUBI:100:6/r9.claim: In the Kināna dialect kanūd means miserly and bad in one’s treatment of dependents; Muqātil gives this view too.
QURTUBI:100:6/r9.anchor: وبلسان كنانة : البخيل السيء الملكة ،   وقاله مقاتل

QURTUBI:100:6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r10.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI:100:6/r10.claim: A poetic usage glosses kanūd as ungrateful toward people’s favors.
QURTUBI:100:6/r10.anchor: كنودٌ لنعماءِ الرجال ومن يكن *** كَنُودًا لنعماءِ الرجال يُبَعَّدِ

QURTUBI:100:6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:100:6/r11.claim: Another gloss says the kanūd rejects small favors and fails to thank for much.
QURTUBI:100:6/r11.anchor: ثم قيل : هو الذي يكفر باليسير ،   ولا يشكر الكثير

QURTUBI:100:6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:100:6/r12.claim: Another view defines kanūd as one who denies the truth.

QURTUBI:100:6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r13.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:100:6/r13.claim: A wordplay says the tribe Kinda was named so because it denied its father.
QURTUBI:100:6/r13.anchor: وقيل : إنما سميت كندة كندة ؛ لأنها جحدت أباها

QURTUBI:100:6/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r14.speaker: إبراهيم بن هرمة
QURTUBI:100:6/r14.claim: Ibrāhīm b. Hirma’s verse uses kanūd for a miserly woman whose stinginess is remembered.
QURTUBI:100:6/r14.anchor: وقال إبراهيم بن هرمة الشاعر : دعِ البُخَلاَءَ إن شمخُوا وصَدُّوا*** وذكرَى بُخْلٍ غانيةٍ كَنودِ

QURTUBI:100:6/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI:100:6/r15.claim: Another etymology derives kanūd from cutting: the ungrateful person cuts off the thanks that should be maintained; kand al-ḥabl means to cut a rope.
QURTUBI:100:6/r15.anchor: وقيل : الكنود من كند إذا قطع ،   كأنه يقطع ما ينبغي أن يواصله من الشكر

QURTUBI:100:6/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r16.speaker: الأعشى
QURTUBI:100:6/r16.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line uses kannādah in a context of cutting, evidence for the root’s sense of severing.
QURTUBI:100:6/r16.anchor: تُمِيطِي بصُلْبِ الفؤاد *** وَصُولِ حبالٍ وكَنَّادَهَا

QURTUBI:100:6/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI:100:6/r17.claim: Kand yaknud means to deny a blessing; kanūd is the masculine form, and kanūd or kand can also describe a woman.
QURTUBI:100:6/r17.anchor: فهو كنود .   وامرأة كنود أيضا ،   وكند مثله

QURTUBI:100:6/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r18.speaker: الأعشى
QURTUBI:100:6/r18.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s verse calls a woman kanūd toward the regular visitor’s affection, ungrateful for continued connection.
QURTUBI:100:6/r18.anchor: أَحْدِثْ لها تُحْدِثْ لوصلكَ إنَّهَا *** كُنُدٌ لوصل الزائر المعتاد

QURTUBI:100:6/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:100:6/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes “the human” here to mean the unbeliever and compares him to barren ground that grows nothing.
QURTUBI:100:6/r19.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : الإنسان هنا الكافر ،   يقول : إنه لكفور

QURTUBI:100:6/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r20.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI:100:6/r20.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the verse was revealed about al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra.
QURTUBI:100:6/r20.anchor: وقال الضحاك : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

QURTUBI:100:6/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r21.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI:100:6/r21.claim: Al-Mubarrad defines kanūd as one who withholds what is due and cites a poem about being kanūd toward a visitor’s affection.

QURTUBI:100:6/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r22.speaker: أبو بكر الواسطي
QURTUBI:100:6/r22.claim: Abū Bakr al-Wāsiṭī defines the kanūd as one who spends God’s blessings in disobedience to God.
QURTUBI:100:6/r22.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الواسطي : الكنود : الذي ينفق نعم الله

QURTUBI:100:6/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r23.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
QURTUBI:100:6/r23.claim: Abū Bakr al-Warrāq says the kanūd attributes blessings to himself and his helpers.
QURTUBI:100:6/r23.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق : الكنود : الذي يرى النعمة من نفسه

QURTUBI:100:6/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r24.speaker: الترمذي
QURTUBI:100:6/r24.claim: Al-Tirmidhī defines the kanūd as one who sees the blessing but not the Benefactor.
QURTUBI:100:6/r24.anchor: وقال الترمذي : الذي يرى النعمة ،   ولا يرى المنعم

QURTUBI:100:6/r25.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r25.speaker: ذو النون المصري
QURTUBI:100:6/r25.claim: Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī says both the halūʿ and kanūd see the blessing but not its giver.
QURTUBI:100:6/r25.anchor: وقال ذو النون المصري : الهلوع والكنود : هو الذي يرى النعمة

QURTUBI:100:6/r26.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r26.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:100:6/r26.claim: Another interpretation calls the kanūd resentful and envious.

QURTUBI:100:6/r27.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r27.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:100:6/r27.claim: Another view calls him ignorant of his own worth; a maxim says that one who fails to know his worth exposes his veil.
QURTUBI:100:6/r27.anchor: وقيل : هو الجهول لقدره .   وفي الحكمة : من جهل قدره هتك ستره

QURTUBI:100:6/r28.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:100:6/r28.speaker: author
QURTUBI:100:6/r28.claim: All the views return to ingratitude and denial; if sound, the Prophet’s interpretation through blameworthy traits is the highest and settles the matter.
QURTUBI:100:6/r28.anchor: قلت : هذه الأقوال كلها ترجع إلى معنى الكفران والجحود

RAZI:100:6/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:6/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:100:6/r1.claim: This is the first of three matters asserted in the oath's response.
RAZI:100:6/r1.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى لما ذكر المقسم به ، ذكر المقسم عليه وهو أمور ثلاثة : ( أحدها ) قوله : { إن الإنسان لربه لكنود }

RAZI:100:6/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:6/r2.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI:100:6/r2.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says kanūd fundamentally means withholding what is due or good; barren land is also called kanūd because it produces nothing.
RAZI:100:6/r2.anchor: قال الواحدي : أصل الكنود منع الحق والخير والكنود الذي يمنع ما عليه ، والأرض الكنود هي التي لا تنبت شيئا

RAZI:100:6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:6/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة والضحاك وقتادة
RAZI:100:6/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Qatāda gloss kanūd as intensely ungrateful; the tribal name Kinda is linked to a man who left his father.
RAZI:100:6/r3.anchor: فقال ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة والضحاك وقتادة : الكنود هو الكفور قالوا : ومنه سمي الرجل المشهور كندة لأنه كند أباه ففارقه

RAZI:100:6/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:6/r4.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI:100:6/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī gives regional glosses: disobedient in Kinda's speech, miserly among Banū Mālik, and ungrateful among Muḍar and Rabīʿa.
RAZI:100:6/r4.anchor: عن الكلبي الكنود بلسان كندة العاصي وبلسان بني مالك

RAZI:100:6/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:6/r5.speaker: النبي
RAZI:100:6/r5.claim: A report from Abū Umāma, tracing the statement to the Prophet, defines kanūd as ungrateful, withholding help, eating alone, and beating his servant.
RAZI:100:6/r5.anchor: وروى أبو أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن : ( الكنود ) هو الكفور الذي يمنع رفده ، ويأكل وحده ، ويضرب عبده

RAZI:100:6/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:6/r6.speaker: الحسن
RAZI:100:6/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the kanūd complains against his Lord, counts misfortunes, and forgets blessings and ease, as in 89:16.
RAZI:100:6/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن : ( الكنود ) اللوام لربه يعد المحن والمصائب ، وينسى النعم والراحات ، وهو كقوله : { وأما إذا ما ابتلاه فقدره عليه رزقه فيقول ربي أهانن }

RAZI:100:6/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:6/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:100:6/r7.claim: Razi says kanūd must denote disbelief or sinfulness; it cannot describe every individual unless it means humanity's natural disposition absent God's protection and guidance, otherwise it refers to a particular disbeliever.
RAZI:100:6/r7.anchor: واعلم أن معنى الكنود لا يخرج عن أن يكون كفرا أو فسقا ، وكيفما كان فلا يمكن حمله على كل الناس ، فلابد من صرفه إلى كافر معين

RAZI:100:6/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:6/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:100:6/r8.claim: The majority's specific-disbeliever reading is supported by Ibn ʿAbbās's report that the sūra was revealed about Qurṭ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Nawfal al-Qurashī.
RAZI:100:6/r8.anchor: والأول قول الأكثرين قالوا : لأن ابن عباس قال : إنها نزلت في قرط بن عبد الله بن عمرو بن نوفل القرشي

RAZI:100:6/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:100:6/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:100:6/r9.claim: Razi says the following question about the dead being raised suits an unbeliever, since it signals denial of resurrection.
RAZI:100:6/r9.anchor: وأيضا فقوله : { أفلا يعلم إذا بعثر ما في القبور } لا يليق إلا بالكافر

QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r12.claim: The statement that humans are ungrateful to their Lord is the answer to the oath.

QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r19.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r19.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r19.claim: Kanud can mean someone who notices afflictions but not blessings.
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r19.anchor: هو الذي يرى ما إليه من البلوى

QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r20.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r20.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r20.claim: Kanud can mean someone resting on the cushion of blessing while his heart remains heedless.
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r20.anchor: هو الذي رأسه على وسادة النعمة

QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r21.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r21.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r21.claim: Kanud can mean someone who forgets blessings and counts misfortunes.

FARRA:v3p284#2/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p284#2/r10.speaker: الكلبي
FARRA:v3p284#2/r10.claim: Al-Kalbi says kanud means ungrateful for blessings in the dialect of Kinda and Hadramawt.
FARRA:v3p284#2/r10.anchor: قال الكلبي وزعم أنها في لغة كندة وحضرموت

MAJAZ:v2p307/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p307/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p307/r5.claim: Kanud means ungrateful; barren earth that produces nothing is also called kanud.
MAJAZ:v2p307/r5.anchor: لكفور وكذلك الأرض الكنود التي لا تنبت شيئا

MAJAZ:v2p307/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p307/r6.speaker: الأعشى
MAJAZ:v2p307/r6.claim: Al-Aʿsha's verse uses kand for something unreceptive to the regular visitor's connection, illustrating barrenness or ingratitude.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p416/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p416/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p416/r1.claim: The oath sworn by horses is evidence for the later premise that man is ungrateful to his Lord.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p416/r1.anchor: this oath sworn by the horses is a testimony to the ungratefulness of man

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p417/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p417/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p417/r3.claim: Kanūd means ungrateful: a person who witnesses horses' obedience and benefits from their sacrifice yet ignores his own duty to God is more ungrateful than animals that know a master's rights.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p417/r3.anchor: an ungrateful person who does not value the favours of his Lord

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p417/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p417/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p417/r4.claim: Horses exemplify service found throughout animals God placed at man's disposal; Qur'anic mentions, especially of camels, should awaken gratitude and teach submission, diligence, and patience.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p417/r4.anchor: camels are mentioned at numerous places

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r1.claim: Horses are singled out because clans needed high-pedigree warhorses for attack, defense, and family protection; their importance also made them common in classical poetry.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r1.anchor: they had great importance in launching an onslaught on the enemy

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r2.claim: The author cites a Ḥamāsī poet's verse about spending on a thoroughbred horse as a house sentinel and keeping a servant for it, illustrating horses' esteem.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r2.anchor: I am restricting myself to just one couplet

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r3.claim: People understand a servant's value from its service, yet man disobeys his Lord and still expects the greatest afterlife reward; horses serve only because God subjected them to man.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r3.anchor: the real value of a servant depends on his services

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r4.claim: Unlike horses, man remains indifferent to worshipping and serving the Creator who made him, all useful animals, and every means of his sustenance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r4.anchor: all other animals who are of use to him

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r11.claim: Kanūd means ungrateful for a blessing; an unnamed poet applies it to someone ungrateful for men's generosity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r11.anchor: الكنود: الكفور للنعمة، قال الشاعر: كنود لنعماء الرجال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives dialectal senses: disobedient in Kinda and Ḥaḍramawt, ungrateful in Rabīʿa and Muḍar, and miserly with poor management in Kināna.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r12.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: الكنود، بلسان كندة وحضر موت: العاصي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r13.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r13.claim: Muqātil identifies the Kināna dialect sense as a miser with bad stewardship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r13.anchor: وبلسان كنانة: البخيل السيء الملكة، وقاله مقاتل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r14.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r14.claim: Al-Kalbī gives the same dialect account except that he assigns the miserly sense to Banū Mālik and omits Ḥaḍramawt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r14.anchor: وقال الكلبي مثله إلا أنه قال: وبلسان بني مالك: البخيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r1.speaker: أبو زبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r1.claim: Abū Zubayd's line uses kanūd of a miserly age or fate, continuing the lexical evidence for the word.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r1.anchor: إن تفتني فلم أطب عنك نفسا ... غير أني أمنى بدهر كنود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r6.claim: A prophetic report describes the kanūd as one who eats alone, withholds help, and beats his servant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث: «الكنود يأكل وحده ويمنع رفده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan define kanūd as denying God's blessings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن: هو الجحود لنعمة الله تعالى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r8.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan also describes the kanūd as one who counts wrongs against his Lord and forgets good deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r8.anchor: وعن الحسن أيضا: هو اللائم لربه، يعد السيئات وينسى الحسنات.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r9.speaker: الفضيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r9.claim: Al-Fuḍayl says the kanūd lets one sin erase many good deeds from memory and treats God as a transaction partner.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r9.anchor: وقال الفضيل: هو الذي تنسيه سيئة واحدة حسنات كثيرة، ويعامل الله على عقد عوض.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r10.speaker: عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r10.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the kanūd withholds help from his people in calamities.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r10.anchor: وقال عطاء: هو الذي لا يعطي في النائبات مع قومه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r11.claim: Another interpretation defines kanūd as miserly; Ibn Qutayba uses barren land that grows nothing as a lexical analogy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r11.anchor: وقيل: البخيل. وقال ابن قتيبة: أرض كنود: لا تنبت شيئا.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r1.claim: The surah warns that most people will perish at the upheaval because they prefer fleeting status and wealth to what endures with God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r1.anchor: إعلام بأن أكثر الخلق يوم الزلزلة هالك لإيثار الفاني من العز والمال على الباقي عند ذي الجلال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r2.claim: The oath, its object, and what follows disclose this purpose; the title is especially apt because the oath and its answer point to it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r2.anchor: وقد علم أن اسمها أدل شيء على ذلك لما هدى إليه القسم والمقسم عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r1.claim: Following al-Zalzalah's account of judgment, this surah traces the disposition that produces evil deeds and the imagined worldly gain that sustains it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r1.anchor: ختم الزلزلة بالجزاء لأعمال الشر يوم الفصل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r2.claim: The oath rebukes people who fail to prepare for Judgment, prefer this life to the next, and treat God's blessings without gratitude.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r2.anchor: موبخا من لا يستعد لذلك اليوم بالاحتراز التام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r9.claim: The surah condemns traits leading to loss in the afterlife, especially prevalent among pagans and hypocrites, and warns Muslims against them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r9.anchor: ذم خصال تفضي بأصحابها إلى الخسران في الآخرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r1.speaker: الفضيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r1.claim: Al-Fudayl defines the ungrateful person as one whose single sin makes him forget many good deeds and who treats God as if owed a return.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514#2/r1.anchor: وقال الفضيل: الكنود الذي تنسيه سيئة واحدة حسنات كثيرة ويعامل الله على عقد عوض

JISHUMI:v10p7511/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r1.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة وقتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r1.claim: Al-Hasan, ʿIkrimah, and Qatadah say the surah is Meccan; another view says it is Medinan and was revealed around a raid.
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r1.anchor: قيل: إنها مكية، عن الحسن، وعكرمة، وقتادة. وقيل: مدنية، وقالوا: نزلت عند جهاد وقع في سرية.

JISHUMI:v10p7511/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r2.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for reciting the surah for every person who spent the night at Muzdalifah and witnessed Jamʿ.
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r2.anchor: من قرأ سورة (والعاديات) أعطي من الأجر عشر حسنات بعدد من بات بالمزدلفة وشهد جمعا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r17.claim: Kanūd means ungrateful; the term is etymologically associated with Kinda rejecting its father.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r17.anchor: الكنود : الكفور . وكند النعمة كنودا . ومنه سمي : كندة ، لأنه كند أباه ففارقه .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r18.speaker: الكلبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r18.claim: Al-Kalbi says kanūd means rebellious in Kinda dialect, miserly among Banu Malik, and ungrateful among Mudar and Rabiʿah.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r18.anchor: وعن الكلبي : الكنود بلسان كندة : العاصي ، وبلسان بني مالك : البخيل ، وبلسان مضر وربيعة : الكفور

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r19.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r19.claim: The human being is especially ungrateful to his Lord, since neglecting gratitude for other benefactors is less serious when their favors are more immediate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r19.anchor: يعني : أنه لنعمة ربه خصوصا لشديد الكفران ؛ لأن تفريطه في شكر نعمة غير الله تفريط قريب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r8.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for reciting al-ʿĀdiyāt for every person who spent the night at Muzdalifah and witnessed Jamʿ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r8.anchor: ( 1335 ) ( من قرأ سورة والعاديات أعطي من الأجر عشر حسنات بعدد من بات بالمزدلفة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327/r1.claim: The following Sūrat al-Qāriʿah is Meccan according to all the authorities mentioned.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327/r1.anchor: سورة القارعة مكية في قولهم جميعا

MUQATIL:100:1-6/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:100:1-6/r8.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:100:1-6/r8.claim: The verse is said to have been revealed about Qurṭ ibn Abd Allah, who ate alone, filled himself while starving his servant, and gave nothing to his people; in Kinana usage kanūd means ungrateful.
MUQATIL:100:1-6/r8.anchor: نزلت في قرط بن عبدالله بن عمرو بن نوفل القرشي، وهو الرجل الذي أكل وحده، وأشبع بطنه وأجاع عبده

QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r1.claim: The Meccan surah has eleven verses and moves in rapid, forceful jumps before settling at its ending, like a runner reaching the finish.
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r1.anchor: سورة العاديات مكية وآياتها إحدى عشرة يجري سياق هذه السورة في لمسات سريعة عنيفة مثيرة

QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r3.claim: A second scene turns from the charge to human ingratitude, denial, selfishness, and intense miserliness.
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r3.anchor: يليه مشهد في النفس من الكنود والجحود والأثرة والشح الشديد

QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r6.claim: The rough, rumbling, cracking rhythm suits the noisy dust and forceful disclosure of graves and hearts, as well as the surah’s ingratitude and greed.
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r6.anchor: والإيقاع الموسيقي فيه خشونة ودمدمة وفرقعة ، تناسب الجو الصاخب المعفر

RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r9.speaker: أبي عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r9.claim: A report attributed to Ubay and raised to the Prophet promises a reward measured by the number who spend a night at Muzdalifah and witness Jamʿ.
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r9.anchor: ويتأكد هذا القول بما روى أبي في فضل السورة مرفوعا : ( من قرأها أعطى من الأجر

TABRISI:100:1/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:100:1/r9.claim: Kanūd means ungrateful; a barren land is also kanūd because it withholds produce, with a root sense of withholding right and good.
TABRISI:100:1/r9.anchor: والكنود الكفور ومنه الأرض الكنود وهي التي لا تنبت شيئا

TABRISI:100:1/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1/r10.speaker: الأعشى
TABRISI:100:1/r10.claim: Al-Aʿshā uses kand for one who is unfaithful to a habitual visitor's affection.
TABRISI:100:1/r10.anchor: قال الأعشى: أحدث لها تحدث لوصلك إنها كند لوصل الزائر المعتاد

TABRISI:100:1/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:100:1/r11.claim: One account derives the name Kinda from severing a relationship.
TABRISI:100:1/r11.anchor: وقيل إنما سميت كندة لقطعها إياها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:100:1-8/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:100:1-8/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:100:1-8/r6.claim: The oath's answer is that humans are ungrateful and deny God's blessings.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:100:1-8/r6.anchor: { إن الإنسان } جواب القسم { لربه لكنود } لكفور.
